title: Pricing & Packaging — token math scratchpad (v4)
content:
Goal: quick back-of-envelope to sanity-check per-token pricing bands and possible starter tiers. Rough, lots of assumptions.

Assumptions:
- Host model: open Llama-like baseline (quantized) for hosted API; avg token cost (infra) ~= $0.00003 / token for generation workloads at scale (ballpark after batching + quantization).
- Embeddings model cost higher per token due to longer context + expensive layers; approximate infra cost ~= $0.00004 / token.
- Average customer request sizes:
  - Short chat reply: 150 prompt tokens + 50 generated = 200 tokens total (we bill input+output)
  - Long chat session Req: 800 prompt + 200 generated = 1000 tokens
  - Embedding per doc: 1500 tokens average (longish docs)
- Target gross margin: 60%+ on hosted API (to cover SRE, support, dev).

Simple per-M token math (generation):
- Infra cost per token: $0.00003
- Infra cost per 1M tokens = $30
- To hit 60% gross margin, price per 1M tokens = $30 / (1 - 0.6) = $75 -> $0.000075 / token.
- Round to $0.00008/token (per-token price) => $80 per 1M tokens.

Embeddings (per-M token):
- Infra cost per token: $0.00004 -> $40 / 1M
- Price for 60% margin: $40 / 0.4 = $100 per 1M tokens -> $0.0001/token.
- But market tends to price embeddings differently (per embedding call or per vector). Consider converting to price per 1k vectors or per 1k tokens.

Per-call math (example):
- Short chat (200 tokens): cost to Redwood infra = 200 * $0.00003 = $0.006 -> price = 200 * $0.00008 = $0.016 -> Redwood margin per call = $0.01 (66%).
- Long chat (1k tokens): infra cost = $0.03 -> price = $0.08 -> margin = $0.05 (62%).

Tier ideas (hosted API):
- Free (dev): 0-50k tokens / month, limited rate, strict fair-use.
- Starter: $20/month -> includes 250k tokens (=> effective $80 / 1M tokens). Overage billed at $0.00009/token.
- Growth: $250/month -> includes 5M tokens (effective $50 / 1M tokens discounted for committed usage). Overage at $0.00007/token.
- Scale: $1,200/month -> includes 30M tokens + better rate limits + SLO credits.
- Enterprise: custom (dedicated, committed capacity). Reserved capacity discounts (dedicated pricing) should be ~30-50% below hosted list depending on term/commit.

Notes on pricing shape:
- Keep public hosted price simple: $0.00008/token generation; $0.00010/token embeddings (or equivalent per 1k embedding vectors). Offer committed discounts via packages to upsell.
- Offer burst/bandwidth limits for Starter to protect backend.

Dedicated / Private considerations:
- Dedicated infra unit economics change: fixed infra + ops. For committed contract, we can price by GPU-hour + ops + margin. Simpler to present as "reserved qps" or "units" with included tokens estimate.
- Example: typical 80GB A100 pool cost to Redwood + ops + amortization -> target revenue $X/month supporting Y tokens -> compute per token equivalent and show 30-50% discount vs hosted. (Need actual infra model to finalize.)

Sensitivity checks:
- If infra cost per token drops to $0.00002 (better quant / batching), hosted price at 60% margin -> $50 / 1M tokens. Could lower Starter price / increase margin.
- If embeddings infra cost is actually $0.00006/token (weird large context), then need to charge $150 / 1M to hit margins -> likely need per-embedding pricing (per-vector) or raise embedding list price.

Operational levers to protect margins:
- Automatic batching + prefix caching: reduces effective tokens served (saves cost) for multi-turn sessions.
- Quantization recommendations for customers with cost sensitivity.
- Soft rate limits + throttles on free/starter tiers.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Get real infra cost model from infra team (per-model, per-hardware, per-quantization profile). Linked ticket: JIRA-PI-42.
- Decide whether to bill input tokens or only output tokens (we currently plan to bill both; confirm competitive signal).
- Embeddings: map to per-vector pricing (e.g., $0.001 / 1k vectors) vs per-token. Need to compute average tokens->vectors mapping for typical customers.
- Starter package sizing: is 250k tokens / $20 too small? Compare to competitor free/paid thresholds.
- How do credits convert to Dedicated reservations? Include conversion math in sales playbook.

Quick scenarios (monthly spend):
- Small startup: 5k gen tokens/day (~150k/month) -> Starter $20 fits.
- SMB: 200k gen tokens/day (~6M/month) -> Growth $250 (5M included) + overage ~1M * $0.00007 = $70 -> total ~$320. Effective price ~ $53 / 1M tokens.

Non-obvious: we should consider per-request pricing for high-RT customers (e.g., long context retrieval + rerank pipelines) since token-only pricing hides inference complexity (reranking has N times cost). Perhaps add guidance for multi-step pipelines: show equivalent token multiplier (e.g., embedding + rerank + generate = 3x tokens).

Notes to self: turn this into a spreadsheet with input sliders: infra cost per token (gen/emb), avg tokens per request, desired margin, and compute recommended list price and tier breakpoints. Share with @Maya for sanity-check.

-- Ethan
